messages:
oncall-bot: Paging @oncall: multiple 5xx spikes and elevated latency for inference and health-checks in AWS region us-west-2a. Alert: ELB target-group unhealthy ratio > 30% across a subset of AZs.

alice: seeing request lat p50 jump to 1.2s and p95 ~4.8s, errors are HTTP 502/504 from our edge ELBs. Dashboards show backend EC2 connection resets.

ben: confirming. CloudWatch: high ENI retransmits in us-west-2a, network RX drops on instances in tg-inference-prod-02.

carla: is this correlated with any recent deploy? I don't see any canary rollouts in the last 2hrs.

dave: no deploys. Autoscaling also hasn't triggered. Looks like a networking problem inside the AZ.

aws-status-bot: AWS Notice — We are investigating increased network packet loss impacting EC2 and ELB in us-west-2a. (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/EC2/12345)

alice: OK, triage plan: 1) shift traffic away from us-west-2a to other AZs/regions, 2) disable AZ routing for ELB and re-register targets in healthy AZs, 3) inform customers.

ben: doing step 1: updating Route53 weight for inference.prodigy.redwood.ai set us-west-2a -> 0, us-west-2b -> 50, us-west-2c -> 50. I'll post the change.

ben: (command)
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.prodigy.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2a","Weight":0,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"1.2.3.4"}]}}]}'
```

carla: added a temporary ELB-level cross-zone load-balancing override and set connection draining to 300s for safe draining of in-progress requests.

dave: started draining targets in tg-inference-prod-02 (us-west-2a). Will monitor connection counts.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3423, severity: Sev2 — Partial regional service degradation. oncall: @alice, runbook: network-az-degradation.

alice: rolling change to routing should take effect in ~1min (Route53 TTL=60). Watching logs.

sre-robin: quick check — can we confirm this is not our BGP/prefix issue? I see no edge route flaps in the border routers. Also nothing from transit gateway.

ben: confirmed BGP stable. Problem looks internal to AWS AZ fabric — ENI error counters and EC2 kernel logs show repeated 'NETDEV WATCHDOG' and tx hang messages.

carla: customer signal: Support queue shows 12 reports in last 20m about slow generation and timeouts. Tagging customer-impact. inc-comm please prepare comms.

inc-comm: drafting update: "We are investigating increased latency and errors in us-west-2 affecting some inference requests. Traffic has been shifted to healthy AZs and mitigation is in progress." Will post to status page when you confirm.

alice: health checks are improving for targets in us-west-2b/c. Backend error rate down from 35% to 4% since traffic shift. Good.

dave: one oddity: a couple of instances in us-west-2a stayed in draining state due to long-lived streaming responses. Increasing ELB idle timeout to 120s helped free sockets.

ben: I've also created an automated fallback route in our smart-router policy to prefer us-west-2b/c for the next 60m. Config snippet: 
```
router.policies.fallback = [{"region":"us-west-2b","weight":0.5},{"region":"us-west-2c","weight":0.5}]
```

sre-robin: good. Also enabling extra KV-cache replication for quick warmups in new AZs.

alice: customer impact: approximate affected traffic 18% of production requests during the event window. Noted for postmortem.

inc-comm: posted status update: "Mitigation: traffic rerouted from the impacted AZ; error rates are decreasing. AWS investigating root cause." (link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-3423) :loudspeaker: 

aws-status-bot: AWS update — Root cause: localized network device within us-west-2a causing packet drops; mitigation: AWS is replacing affected network hardware. ETA unknown.

carla: action items while AWS remediates: 1) keep weights off us-west-2a for 2 hours, 2) bump capacity in 2b/c if latency rises, 3) keep ELB draining until sockets clear.

ben: scaling up extra inference instances in 2b/c now (ASG increase +20%).

alice: handoff at 40m: I'll be off for the next 2hrs. @dave — you're oncall for mitigation window. Please confirm monitoring and customer comms.

dave: taking handoff. I've enabled additional dashboards and set an alert to notify if p95 > 2s or errors > 5% in any region.

sre-robin: collecting instance-level logs from problematic hosts in us-west-2a and saved snapshots to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-3423/logs.tar.gz

carla: support triage note: prioritize customers with committed SLAs and jobs running >5m. Created internal ticket SUPPORT-7931.

alice: final note before leaving: include this in postmortem: timeline, Route53 change, ELB draining, AWS hardware replacement, traffic % affected, customer-reports count, and any config changes we made.

dave: ack. Will run postmortem template and tag owners. Marking incident as Mitigated for now — keeping watch.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-3423 status: Mitigated (monitoring). Severity downgraded to Sev3. Updates will follow in the incident doc.

inc-comm: publishing final update to customers: "Issue mitigated. AWS reports hardware replacement underway in the impacted AZ. If you still see errors, please contact support with your request ID."

aws-status-bot: AWS final update — hardware replaced and network fabric showing normal metrics for us-west-2a. Monitoring continues.

carla: reintroducing us-west-2a into Route53 over a 15m ramp starting now, with health-check gating.

ben: weight ramp command posted and healthchecks green. Traffic back to normal distribution.

alice: thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: @dave. Please include remediation and think about automating route53 reroutes for future AZ-level network spikes.

dave: will do. Closing realtime thread.
